messages:
claudia: Heads up — saw a pattern of Xid 31 followed by reboots on prod-gpu-3 this morning. Thinking we should centralize dmesg/journalctl + periodic nvidia-smi snapshots into a small ingest pipeline to speed triage.
ryan: +1. current flow is painful — logs live on node, we SSH to pull. fluent-bit or a tiny cron that POSTs snapshots would help.
mike: can we capture kernel oops + ECC counters? often the useful bits are in dmesg within 10s of Xid.
claudia: proposal: on driver Xid event, run a collector that grabs `dmesg -T | tail -n 200`, `journalctl -k -n 200`, `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER`, and a short `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,serial,uuid,name --format=csv`. Upload compressed payload to logs topic with node metadata.
oliver: sounds good. a couple questions: frequency throttling (so we don't flood on noisy nodes) and retention/cost model. also dedupe identical dumps before ingest.
infra-bot: Alert: node prod-gpu-3 reported Xid 31 at 2026-03-18T08:12:05Z
sara: can we include a short content-hash of the last 500 lines so parsers can group duplicates? :thumbsup:
ryan: quick collector sketch: ```#!/bin/bash
TS=$(date +%s)
NODE=$(hostname -s)
dmesg -T | tail -n 500 > /tmp/dmesg.$TS
journalctl -k -n 500 > /tmp/journal.$TS
nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER -x > /tmp/nvsmi.$TS
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version > /tmp/driver.$TS
zip -j /tmp/gpu_snapshot.$TS.zip /tmp/dmesg.$TS /tmp/journal.$TS /tmp/nvsmi.$TS /tmp/driver.$TS
# POST compressed blob with metadata header
curl -X POST -H "X-Node: $NODE" -H "X-TS: $TS" --data-binary @/tmp/gpu_snapshot.$TS.zip https://logs.internal/gpu/ingest
```
claudia: nice. add rack/tagging metadata (rack id, region, GPU model, driver version) and a trace id so we can correlate with APM and the node's cloud instance id. Also ensure we scrub container IDs or PII.
mike: example dmesg snippet from prod-gpu-3: ```[Mon Mar 18 08:11:58 2026] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=4321, GPU=a100-40gb
[Mon Mar 18 08:12:01 2026] NVRM: GPU fell off the bus
[Mon Mar 18 08:12:02 2026] kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID=0010
```
oliver: parsing idea: build an ingest pipeline that extracts Xid codes, ECC counters, `GPU fell off the bus`, driver version, and fingerprint the stack. Create a composite fingerprint: `<gpu_model>|<driver>|<first_40_chars_of_dmesg_hash>` so we can group recurring hardware failures.
claudia: ops playbook suggestion: if a single physical GPU reports >3 Xid 31 or `GPU fell off the bus` within 24h, automatically mark node degraded, schedule drain+replace, and alert HW team. for 1-2 events, tag as flaky and reduce scheduling weight.
sara: from cost POV: if we snapshot on every Xid and occasional periodic snapshots, estimate ~50GB/day compressed for fleet of 200 nodes. we need S3 + ES/Opensearch indexing costs; i'll model.
ryan: I'll prototype an ES ingest pipeline with a simple ingest processor that runs grok + fingerprinting and sets a `failure_fingerprint` field. POC by EOW.
claudia: also add RBAC for the GPU log index and retention rules (30d hot, 90d warm) and an automated scrub pipeline to remove container IDs. I'll open a GH issue with checklist.
infra-bot: Created issue INFRA-723: 'GPU logroom ingest + fingerprinting' by @claudia
sara: thanks — ping me for the cost modeling and I'll slot it into next week's infra budget review.
claudia: ok — next steps: (1) ryan POC ingest + sample parser, (2) mike & oliver add playbook details and drain logic, (3) sara cost estimate, (4) claudi­a open infra issue and link runbook. anyone else?
ryan: quick follow-up question — do we want realtime alerts only, or a nightly reindex job to find hotspots across 7d windows?
mike: both. realtime for ops, nightly reindex for trend detection and hot-card identification.
claudia: agreed. closing loop for now, i'll post the GH issue link when created. thanks all.
